tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigated Magento admin, logged in, opened Manage Attribute Sets, used the grid filter input to search for 'My Attribute Set', clicked Search, and opened the Edit page. Stable element hashes were recorded for the Set Name filter input (element_hash '987ca07d3f') and the Search button (element_hash '90708cd5ce'). The Edit link was best targeted by an XPath that locates the grid row by exact visible text and clicks the anchor whose href contains the admin edit route.

Task Definition:
- This tool's single, deterministic task is: navigate to the Magento Manage Attribute Sets page, filter the grid by a provided attribute set name, and open that set's Edit page. Authentication is out of scope and must be handled by the caller/session.

Action Plan (ordered deterministic steps):
1) Navigate to the provided admin_url that points to the attribute-sets listing.
2) Wait briefly for the page and grid to render.
3) Confirm the grid is present (extract page content for verification).
4) Input the provided set_name into the Set Name filter using the recorded stable elementHash.
5) Click the Search (Apply Filters) control using the recorded elementHash to apply the filter.
6) Wait for the grid to refresh.
7) Click the Edit link for the row that exactly matches the provided set_name using an XPath that finds the row by visible text and clicks the anchor whose href points to the edit route.
8) Wait for navigation, then extract the Edit page content to confirm success and capture Save/Back controls.

Variable Identification:
- admin_url (string, required): exact full URL to the Manage Attribute Sets page. Using a full page URL avoids relying on sidebar clicks which may be JS-driven.
- set_name (string, required): visible name of the attribute set to find and open. This maps directly to the grid's visible text.
- wait_seconds (number, optional): optional wait time if caller wants to tune timing. Default small waits included in steps.

Step Optimization / Rationale:
- Navigation: direct navigation to the Manage Attribute Sets page is preferred over clicking sidebar links because admin menus may be JS-driven and sensitive to the browser environment. The recorded steps used direct navigation at times and the URL is stable.
- Deterministic Interactions: Use recorded elementHash values for the Set Name filter input ('987ca07d3f') and the Search button ('90708cd5ce') because these were captured from actual interactions and are more stable than positional CSS in the grid header.
- XPath for Edit link: The Edit link target varies by row; an XPath that finds the row by exact visible text and clicks the anchor whose href contains 'catalog_product_set/edit' is deterministic and resistant to row order or pagination.
- Removed non-essential UI steps: The 'Add New Set' button and the Add-New form were observed during recording but are not required for the core task (open existing set for edit). To keep the tool single-purpose and deterministic, Add New Set interaction is omitted here. If a different tool is needed to create sets, a separate tool should be created.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Localization: text-based XPath (matching visible 'Set Name' or the set_name string) can break under different languages. The tool expects the caller to provide the exact display text currently shown in the admin UI.
- Page structure differences: If the admin theme changes table classes or grid structure significantly, the XPath may need adjustment. Mitigation: the tool first extracts page content (manage_attribute_sets_page) so the caller can verify presence of grid and adapt if needed.
- Authentication: caller must ensure the browser/session is authenticated. The tool intentionally does not perform login steps.

Deterministic only: every step is linear and deterministic; there are no optional branches. The tool always attempts to open the Edit page for the provided set_name and reports the resulting page content under 'edit_attribute_set_page'.
name: magento_open_attribute_set_for_edit
description: Navigate to Magento Admin Manage Attribute Sets, filter by attribute set name, and open the attribute set's Edit page for modification. Assumes the automation session is already authenticated with a valid admin session (no login steps).

steps.description: Navigate to the Manage Attribute Sets page. Use the provided admin_url so the tool works across environments.
Short wait to allow the page to load and for the grid controls to render.
Verify page has the Manage Attribute Sets grid and that filter inputs/buttons exist.
steps.goal: Confirm Manage Attribute Sets page loaded (title/header presence) and that grid is present before interacting.

steps.description: Enter the requested attribute set name into the 'Set Name' filter input (deterministic interaction using recorded elementHash).
Click the grid 'Search' / Apply Filters button to apply the Set Name filter (deterministic interaction using recorded elementHash).
Wait for the grid to refresh with the filtered results.
Click the Edit link for the row that exactly matches the provided {set_name}. Uses an XPath that locates the row by visible cell text then clicks the anchor whose href points to the edit route.
Wait for the Edit Attribute Set page to load after clicking the Edit link.
Extract page title and presence of Save/Back controls to verify successful navigation to the Edit view.
steps.goal: Confirm Edit Attribute Set page opened and capture primary edit controls (Save, Back) and form fields (Name, Based On)

input_schema.name: admin_url
input_schema.description: Full URL of the Magento Admin Manage Attribute Sets page (example: "http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/catalog_product_set/"). Must point to the attribute sets listing page.

input_schema.name: set_name
input_schema.description: Exact attribute set display name to locate and open for editing (example: "My Attribute Set"). Matches visible text in the grid.

input_schema.name: wait_seconds
input_schema.description: Milliseconds to wait after navigation and after actions (useful for slower pages). Default automation may use 1-2 seconds; provide a number of seconds if needed.
